input.quote: any dispute, claim or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation or validity thereof, including the determination of the scope or applicability of this Agreement to arbitrate (a "Dispute") that is not resolved within [***] after written notice of the Dispute by one Party to the other shall be determined by arbitration in [***] before [***] arbitrators
input.rationale: Governing law is already at our preferred position: Section 15.5 (p0627) applies New York law (and the Letter, p0671, does the same). The forum, however, fails both preferred and fallback: Section 15.6(a) sends all merits Disputes to mandatory JAMS arbitration with the seat and panel redacted ("arbitration in [***] before [***] arbitrators"), so there is no court forum at all and we cannot confirm the seat is not foreign — walk-away territory if it is. Neither the Delaware/California/London fallback courts nor New York County courts are designated anywhere. We therefore keep New York law and replace only the arbitration referral in Section 15.6(a) with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, conforming the "Dispute" definition and preserving the interim/injunctive relief carve-out in Section 15.6(j). The residual arbitration machinery in Section 15.6(b)-(g) and the page-break fragment in p0630 become inoperative and should be struck in the conforming pass; the subject-matter carve-outs for foreign patent/trademark validity (15.6(h)) and Program Invention ownership (15.6(i)) are customary and left in place.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law already governs, but the merits forum is JAMS arbitration in an undisclosed seat; our position requires the state and federal courts in New York County to have exclusive jurisdiction, with interim relief still available under Section 15.6(j). We have replaced only the arbitration referral in Section 15.6(a) and conformed the "Dispute" definition accordingly; the residual arbitration procedures in Section 15.6(b)-(g) fall away and should be struck in the conforming pass.
